--- title: "The tractoverse" subtitle: "White matter tractography analysis in R" author: - name: "Aymeric Stamm" affiliation: Department of Mathematics Jean Leray, UMR CNRS 6629, Nantes, France date: "2026-11-26" date-format: long format: revealjs: theme: dark logo: Banner-squares.png footer: "Aymeric Stamm  ·  [astamm.github.io/talks](https://astamm.github.io/talks.html)  ·  aymeric.stamm@cnrs.fr  ·  2026-11-26    ![](tractoverse-montage.png){height=24px style='vertical-align:middle;margin-left:6px;'}" slide-number: c/t progress: true width: 1280 height: 720 transition: fade transition-speed: fast code-line-numbers: false highlight-style: dracula fig-align: center css: custom.css title-slide-attributes: data-background-color: "#0d1117" brand: false execute: echo: true eval: false warning: false message: false --- ## The brain's white matter ::: {.cols-2} :::: {.callout style="font-size:0.8em;"} **Diffusion MRI** probes water motion in tissue at the micron scale. - Axons restrict diffusion **along** their axis → **anisotropy** - Magnetic field gradient attenuates the MR signal → diffusion-weighted images - Voxel-level diffusion **model** → local fiber orientation and tissue properties **Tractography** follows these orientations across voxels to reconstruct 3-D fiber trajectories which carry microstructural information. ![Taken from Wikimedia Commons - under [CC BY 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/deed.en) license](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d1/Comparison_between_anatomic_dissections_using_the_fiber_dissection_technique_and_tractography_PMC3640224_figure_F4.jpg){width=60% fig-align="center"} :::: ```{mermaid} %%| echo: false %%| eval: true %%{init:{"theme":"dark","themeVariables":{"fontSize":"16px"}}}%% flowchart TD A["🧠 Diffusion MRI
(raw signal)"]:::blue --> B["Preprocessing
(Eddy, motion, B0)"]:::grey B --> C["Diffusion model
(DTI, CSD, NODDI…)"]:::blue C --> D["Tractography algorithm
(deterministic / probabilistic)"]:::blue D --> E["🔗 Streamlines
(ordered 3-D points)"]:::green E --> F1["Tractometry
(microstructure along tract)"]:::teal E --> F2["Connectomics
(region-to-region graph)"]:::teal E --> F3["Shape analysis
(FDA, optimal transport)"]:::teal classDef blue fill:#1c3d5a,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#e6edf3 classDef green fill:#1a3a2a,stroke:#3fb950,color:#e6edf3 classDef teal fill:#1a3035,stroke:#39c5cf,color:#e6edf3 classDef grey fill:#21262d,stroke:#8b949e,color:#8b949e ``` ::: --- ## The R gap ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="40%"} :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} **Major tractography tools** — none in R: | Software | Language | Analysis? | |:---------|:---------|:---------:| | MRtrix3 | C++ | Connectomics | | DIPY | Python | Connectomics + Tractometry | | pyAFQ | Python | Tractometry | | Scilpy | Python | Connectomics + Tractometry | | DSI Studio | C++ | Connectomics | *(15+ tools surveyed — **0 in R**)* :::: ::: ::: {.column width="10%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} **R packages on CRAN** for diffusion MRI:
dti — diffusion tensor fitting only, GPL, **47** dependencies
tractor.base — preprocessing pipeline, no streamline analysis
dmri.tracking — archived ✗
No R package provides comprehensively: streamline objects tractometry connectomics shape analysis 3-D visualization microstructure simulation :::: ::: ::: --- ## The tractoverse :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} A **modular** collection of R packages for tractography analysis — inspired by the tidyverse. :::: :::: {style="width:70%; margin:0 auto; font-size:0.68em;"} | Package | CRAN | Version | Role | |:--------|:----:|:-------:|:-----| | fiber | ✅ | 0.3.0 | Data structures | | riot | ✅ | 1.2.0 | I/O (rvtk unblocked) | | rtists | ⏳ | 0.1.0 | 3-D visualization | | toad | ⏳ | 0.1.0 | Reference datasets | | master | 🔜 | dev | Microstructure sim | | bot | 🔜 | dev | Optimal transport | | tractoverse | 🔜 | dev | Meta-package |
+ rvtk — VTK infrastructure for R (v0.2.0 on CRAN)  |  master will fold in midi (on CRAN)

:::: --- ## `fiber` — S7 data structures {.section-header} :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} **The backbone** of the tractoverse. Like `tibble` is to the tidyverse. Three [S7](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/) classes: :::: ::: {.cols-2} :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"}
streamline — one tract
@points ($P \times 3$ matrix)
@point_data (list of length-$P$ numeric vectors)
@streamline_data (list of scalars)
bundle — collection of streamlines
@streamlines (list of $S$ streamlines)
@streamline_data (list of length-$S$ numeric vectors)
@bundle_data (list of scalars)
bundle_set — multi-subject / multi-session
@bundles (list of $B$ bundles)
@bundle_data (list of length-$B$ numeric vectors)
@set_data (list of scalars)
:::: :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"}
Data lifting and subsetting
✅ @streamline_data common to all streamlines in a bundle → **lifted** to @streamline_data of the bundle;
✅ @bundle_data common to all bundles in a set → **lifted** to @set_data of the bundle set.
✅ Upon subsetting, lifted data is **propagated down** to the lower-level objects.
:::: ::: --- ## `fiber` — quick start ```r library(fiber) t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 50) # Build a helix streamline sl <- streamline( points = cbind(X = cos(t), Y = sin(t), Z = t / (2 * pi)), point_data = list(FA = runif(50, 0.3, 0.9)) ) sl #> ── Object of class `fiber::streamline()` with 50 points. ── #> • Point attributes: FA #> • Streamline attributes: none # Geometry on streamlines get_curvilinear_length(sl) #> [1] 6.36 get_sinuosity(sl) #> [1] 6.36 # Build a bundle and reparametrize b <- bundle(lapply(1:10, \(i) reparametrize(sl, n_points = 20L))) b #> ── Object of class `fiber::bundle()` with 10 streamlines [20-20 pts/sl] ── # Multi-subject bundle set bs <- bundle_set(list("sub-01" = b, "sub-02" = b)) bs #> ── Object of class `fiber::bundle_set()` with 2 bundles [10-10 sl/bundle] ── ``` ::: {.callout-box .ok style="margin-top:1rem; font-size:0.7em;"} ✅ On CRAN (0.3.0)  |  📦 Install: `install.packages("fiber")`  |  🔗 [tractoverse.github.io/fiber](https://tractoverse.github.io/fiber/) ::: --- ## `riot` — R I/O for Tractography {.section-header} :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} **Read & write** tractography files in R — like `readr` is to the tidyverse. :::: :::{.cols-2} ::::{style="font-size:0.65em;"} **Supported formats:** | Format | Read | Write | |:-------|:----:|:-----:| | VTK legacy `.vtk` | ✅ | ✅ | | VTK XML `.vtp` | ✅ | ✅ | | medInria `.fds` | ✅ | ✅ | | MRtrix `.tck/.tsf` | ✅ | — | | TrackVis `.trk` | ✅ | — | | DIPY `.dpy` | ✅ | — | **Returns** `fiber::streamline` or `fiber::bundle` objects.
✅ On CRAN (1.2.0) — rvtk (v0.2.0) unblocked the submission.
:::: :::: {style="font-size:0.65em; padding-left:1rem;"} **`rvtk`** — VTK in R (not part of tractoverse) ```{mermaid} %%| echo: false %%| eval: true %%{init:{"theme":"dark"}}%% flowchart LR R["R package
(riot)"] --> rvtk["rvtk
(infrastructure)"] rvtk --> VTK["VTK C++ library
(auto-downloaded)"] style R fill:#1c3d5a,stroke:#58a6ff,color:#e6edf3 style rvtk fill:#2d1f52,stroke:#a371f7,color:#e6edf3 style VTK fill:#1a3a2a,stroke:#3fb950,color:#e6edf3 ``` - Searches for installed VTK or **downloads prebuilt static libs** - No system dependency for end users - `use_rvtk()` sets up any downstream package in one call - On CRAN as `rvtk` v0.2.0 🔗 [astamm.github.io/rvtk](https://astamm.github.io/rvtk/) :::: ::: --- ## `riot` — reading any format ```r library(riot) # VTK (all three sub-formats share the same read_bundle() API) uf_vtk <- read_bundle(system.file("extdata", "UF_left.vtk", package = "riot")) uf_vtp <- read_bundle(system.file("extdata", "UF_left.vtp", package = "riot")) uf_fds <- read_bundle(system.file("extdata", "UF_left.fds", package = "riot")) # MRtrix and TrackVis af_tck <- read_bundle(system.file("extdata", "AF_left.tck", package = "riot")) cc_trk <- read_bundle(system.file("extdata", "CCMid.trk", package = "riot")) af_tck #> # Attach metadata at read time uf_meta <- read_bundle( system.file("extdata", "UF_left.vtk", package = "riot"), bundle_data = list(subject = "sub-01", hemisphere = "left") ) uf_meta@bundle_data #> $subject [1] "sub-01" #> $hemisphere [1] "left" ``` :::{.callout-box style="margin-top:1rem; font-size:0.7em;"} ✅ On CRAN (1.2.0)  |  📦 Install: `install.packages("riot")`  |  🔗 [tractoverse.github.io/riot](https://tractoverse.github.io/riot/) ::: --- ## `rtists` — 3-D visualization {.section-header} :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} **Interactive 3-D** tractography rendering — like `ggplot2` is to the tidyverse. :::: ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} Default backend is a self-contained [**three.js**](https://threejs.org/) htmlwidget (no CDN) → pan, rotate, zoom in any browser, with an on-scene toolbar; [**plotly**](https://plotly.com/r/) kept as interim fallback. **`plot3d()`** is an S7 generic with methods for both `streamline` and `bundle`: | `color =` value | Effect | |:----------------|:-------| | `"orientation"` (default) | RGB from fiber direction | | `@point_data` key | Continuous scale per point | | `@streamline_data` key | Uniform color per tract | | CSS string `"steelblue"` | Fixed color |
⏳ Submitted to CRAN (0.1.0) — awaiting approval
:::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} :::: {style="text-align:center; font-size:0.7em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot3d(sub) # orientation RGB ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Standard DTI color convention: R/G/B = left–right / ant–post / sup–inf :::: ::: ::: --- ## `rtists` — coloring by diffusion metrics ::: {.columns} ::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} :::: {.column width="49%"} ```r # Color by FA (per-point scalar) rtists::plot3d(sub_fa, color = "FA", palette = "Viridis") ``` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot3d(sub_fa, color = "FA", palette = "Viridis", tooltip = FALSE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: :::: :::: {.column width="2%"} :::: :::: {.column width="49%"} ```r # Uniform color per streamline (mean FA) rtists::plot3d(sub_fa, color = "mean_FA", palette = "RdYlBu") ``` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot3d(sub_fa, color = "mean_FA", palette = "RdYlBu", tooltip = FALSE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: :::: ::: ::: ::: {.callout-box style="font-size:0.7em;"} ⏳ Submitted to CRAN (0.1.0) — awaiting approval  |  📦 Install: `pak::pak("tractoverse/rtists")`  |  🔗 [tractoverse.github.io/rtists](https://tractoverse.github.io/rtists/) ::: --- ## `toad` — reference datasets {.section-header} :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} **Tractography Open Atlas Data** *(data package)* — formerly `mascot` :::: ::: {.cols-2} :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} On-demand download, locally cached. All datasets returned as `fiber::bundle` objects. **HCP1065 population atlas** *(CC BY-SA 4.0)* - 87 white matter bundles - Averaged across 1,065 healthy HCP adults - Yeh et al. (2022), Nature Communications **TractSeg per-subject bundles** *(CC BY-NC 4.0)* - 72 tracts × 105 HCP Young Adult subjects - Segmented with [TractSeg](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/TractSeg) - Wasserthal et al. (2018), NeuroImage :::: :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} ```r library(toad) # Browse available bundles available_bundles("HCP1065") #> [1] "Anterior Commissure" "Left Arcuate Fasciculus" ... # Load by name (downloads once, cached) cst_left <- HCP1065_CST_L() cst_left #> ── Object of class `fiber::bundle()` with 5577 streamliness #> and [234–291] points per streamline. ── #> #> • Point attributes: none #> • Streamline attributes: none #> • Bundle attributes: none # Or the generic importer bundle <- import_bundle( dataset = "TractSeg", bundle = "Left Arcuate Fasciculus", subjects = "599469" ) ``` :::: ::: --- ## `toad` — real tractography in a line ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} # Population-average corticospinal tract (left hemisphere) cst <- toad::HCP1065_CST_L() # Keep the embedded widget light: 300 of the 5,577 streamlines sub <- cst[round(seq(1, length(cst), length.out = 300))] # Compute real geometric attributes so the widget can show tooltip + legend sub <- fiber::add_shape_descriptors(sub, c("curvature", "torsion")) # Instantly visualize (hover a tract; toggle the Legend button) plot3d(sub) # orientation RGB ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-box style="font-size:0.7em;"} ⏳ Submitted to CRAN (0.1.0) — awaiting approval  |  📦 Install: `pak::pak("tractoverse/toad")`  |  🔗 [tractoverse.github.io/toad](https://tractoverse.github.io/toad/) ::: --- ## `master` — microstructure simulation {.section-header} ::::{style="font-size:0.7em;"} **Multivariate Axonal Simulator for Tractography Evaluation**, the successor of `midi` (Microstructure Information from Diffusion Imaging). Simulate realistic white-matter bundles with microstructural attributes — used to validate tractography algorithms and design experiments. :::: :::{.columns} ::: {.column width="40%"} ::::{style="font-size:0.7em;"} **Taxonomy of compartments:** - Restricted (cylinders, spheres): model axons - Hindered (tensors): model extra-axonal space - Free (isotropic): model CSF **Each compartment** is an R6 object with method `$get_signal()`. :::: ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::::{style="font-size:0.7em;"} ```r # ------- Define a cylinder compartment (axon model) ------- restr <- VanGelderenCompartment$new( radius = 0.5, # µm diffusivity = 3 # µm²/ms ) cyl <- CylinderCompartment$new( axis = c(0, 0, 1), restricted_compartment = restr ) # ------- Query parameters ------- cyl$get_parameters() #> $CylinderRadius [1] 0.5 #> $CylinderDiffusivity [1] 3 # ------- Compute signal attenuation ------- cyl$get_signal( small_delta = 30, big_delta = 30, G = 0.04, direction = c(0, 0, 1) ) #> [1] 0.002063 ``` :::: ::: ::: ::: {.callout-box .ok style="font-size:0.7em;"} 📌 `midi` (on CRAN) will fold in here  |  🔜 `master` in development  |  📦 Install: `pak::pak("tractoverse/master")`  |  🔗 [tractoverse.github.io/master](https://tractoverse.github.io/master/) ::: --- ## `master` — simulate & explore :::{.cols-2} ::::{style="font-size:0.7em;"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: :::
Show the code ```r pert <- master::pyt_defaults()$perturbation pert$n_axons <- 8L # 8 per branch: 5 parcels x 2 x 8 = 80 streamlines b_left <- master::simulate_pyramidal_tract(perturbation = pert, hemisphere = "left", seed = 7) b_right <- master::simulate_pyramidal_tract(perturbation = pert, hemisphere = "right", seed = 7) b <- fiber::bind_bundle_sets(b_left, b_right) # 10 bundles × 16 streamlines = 160 b |> rtists::plot3d(color = "parcel") ```
:::: ::::{style="font-size:0.7em;"} **Functional-data generative design** — a reference centerline perturbed by smooth random fields of axons: - Centerline: flat central interaction segment + smoothly bending arms - Axons: zero-mean functional random fields in a B-spline basis with exponentially autocorrelated Gaussian coefficients - Pre-assembled configurations via `simulate_scenario()`: bending, fanning, merging, kissing, crossing - Emits `fiber::bundle_set` objects, ready for `rtists::plot3d()`
📌 midi (on CRAN) will fold in here: superimposing diffusion microstructure info (e.g. ellipses) on top of the streamlines

🔗 [astamm.github.io/rvtk](https://astamm.github.io/rvtk/) :::: ::: :::: {style="font-size:0.7em; padding-top:1rem;"} **JSS paper** — in preparation :::: ::::{.callout-box style="font-size:0.7em;"} 🙏 Partly funded by the French Agence Nationale de la Recherche (project ANR-23-CE45-0037). :::: --- ## The tractoverse ecosystem ::: {.cols-2} :::: {style="font-size:0.7em;"} **One modular family** for tractography analysis in R, inspired by the tidyverse. - `fiber` is the **backbone**: S7 data structures shared by every package - `master` simulates, `riot` reads/writes, `rtists` visualizes, `toad` ships reference data - `bot` adds optimal transport (in development) - `rvtk` provides the VTK infrastructure underneath `riot` 🔗 [github.com/tractoverse](https://github.com/tractoverse) :::: :::: {style="background:#fff;border:1px solid #ccc;border-radius:10px;padding:1rem;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;"}

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
